documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Feels back to herself since the November hospitalization. Periods regular again since January. Working 25 hrs/wk at the store. Still no tobacco, alcohol or drugs. Did not end up going to family planning, using condoms.

Exam: normal. Thyroid smooth, not enlarged. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No rashes.
PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 3.

Plan: urine GC/CT (under 25). Pap not due until 2027. Flu this fall. Hgb normal in December, no need to repeat. Physical next spring.

conditions.label: Mature cystic teratoma of right ovary

reports.text: Axial images of the pelvis without IV contrast. Uterus normal in size. Left ovary normal. Right ovary contains a 3 cm well-circumscribed mass. No free fluid, no pelvic lymphadenopathy. Bladder unremarkable. Visualized bones normal.

Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain. No abnormal signal in the cerebral hemispheres, mesial temporal lobes, basal ganglia, brainstem or cerebellum. No restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No mass, hemorrhage or extra-axial collection.

Specimen: right ovarian cyst, laparoscopic cystectomy. Gross: 3.0 cm cyst containing sebaceous material and hair. Microscopic: cyst lined by keratinizing squamous epithelium with skin adnexal structures; mature neural (glial) tissue is present. No immature neuroepithelial elements. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Mature cystic teratoma of the right ovary with mature glial tissue. Negative for immature elements and malignancy.

documents.title: Neurology Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE, regional hospital
Admission 9/7/2025 to 10/3/2025

23-year-old woman, no daily medications, NKDA, with a septic abortion in November 2024 as her only prior history. Brought to the ED by friends after roughly a week of out-of-character behavior: rapid swings in mood, suspiciousness of others and hearing voices. Denied drug and alcohol use. Family history of thyroid autoimmunity (mother) and SLE (maternal aunt).

ED: T 37.8, BP 130/85, HR 102, RR 18. Agitated and disoriented to time and place. Orofacial dyskinesias. No focal weakness; increased tone in the arms with intermittent dystonic posturing.

Workup: LP with CSF WBC 22, RBC 4, protein 56, glucose 60, Gram stain negative, culture no growth. EEG with diffuse slowing, no epileptiform activity. MRI brain normal. CSF NMDA receptor (GluN1) IgG positive, titer 1:32; serum also positive. CT pelvis obtained for tumor search: 3 cm right ovarian mass.

Diagnosis: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis associated with a right ovarian teratoma.

Treatment: methylprednisolone 1 g IV daily x5 days and IVIG 0.4 g/kg daily x5 days, started 9/8. Gynecology performed laparoscopic right ovarian cystectomy on 9/12; pathology mature cystic teratoma with mature glial tissue, no immature elements. Agitation and movements settled over the following three weeks; orientation normal by discharge, with some slowness of recall.

Discharge medications: prednisone 60 mg daily, reduce by 10 mg each week until off.
Disposition: home with her mother. Neurology clinic in 6 to 8 weeks. Gynecology post-op check as scheduled.

documents.title: Call from mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called (pt verbally consented to sharing in a prior visit; mom is her listed emergency contact). Lauren was admitted Sunday through the ED, neurology team thinks it is an autoimmune encephalitis, they found something on her ovary and are planning surgery. Mom wanted the PCP to know. Told her we'd request records and see Lauren after discharge. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Call from mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read. Will see her within a week of discharge, front desk please watch for it.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily, then lower by 10 mg each week as directed until off

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with her mother after a nearly 4 week admission (9/7 to 10/3). Summary not received yet; history from pt, mom, and the discharge paperwork they brought. Diagnosed with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Had steroids and IVIG, and a right ovarian cyst was removed laparoscopically on 9/12; mom says they were told it was a teratoma. Remembers little of the first two weeks.

Now: on prednisone 60 mg, dropping by 10 each week (on 50 starting this weekend). Sleeping 10+ hrs, appetite up. Forgets things she was told a few minutes earlier at times. No hallucinations, no unusual movements since discharge per mom. Not driving yet, mom is driving her. Out of work until neurology sees her.

Exam: calm, pleasant, oriented x3, speech normal, a little slow to answer. No orofacial movements, tone normal, no dystonic posturing. Laparoscopy incisions healing well.

A/P:
1. Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with ovarian teratoma, removed. Recovering. Continue taper exactly as written. Neurology in November, gyn post-op next week.
2. Steroid taper: watch sleep and mood; call for fevers.
3. Work note through 11/30 given.
Records requested. Will see her in early spring, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY, regional hospital
Date of visit: 11/18/2025

Seen for follow-up of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis (GluN1 antibody positive, right ovarian mature teratoma removed 9/12/2025), treated with steroids and IVIG. Prednisone now at 10 mg, last dose this week.

She and her mother report steady improvement. Mood stable, no psychotic symptoms, no abnormal movements. Mild trouble holding on to details at work training videos she is watching at home; otherwise managing daily tasks.

Exam: alert, fully oriented, fluent speech, recalls 3 of 3 objects at 5 minutes with one cue. Cranial nerves intact. Normal tone and strength, no dyskinesias, no dystonia. Gait normal.

Impression: good recovery after first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal.
Plan: finish the taper. No further immunotherapy now. Pelvic ultrasound once a year to look for a new teratoma; gynecology to arrange. Return to work as tolerated. Neurology visit in 6 months, sooner for any return of behavioral change, sleep disruption or movements.

documents.title: work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I started back at work 2 days a week after New Years. My manager wants something saying I can go up to 3 days. Also did neurology send you anything? They said they would.

documents.title: Re: work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're back. Letter for 3 days a week is in your documents tab. We haven't gotten anything from neurology yet, we'll ask them. Please book a visit for late February or March.

documents.title: Re: work
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Neurology clinic notes requested by fax today.

documents.title: Neurology note received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 11/18/25 neurology clinic note arrived today, about three months after the visit and after a second request. Scanned for PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after her encephalitis admission. Neurology note from November reviewed (arrived in February): good recovery, taper to finish, yearly pelvic US for teratoma surveillance via gyn, neuro again in about 6 months.

She finished prednisone right before Thanksgiving week. Working 3 days a week now. Memory "almost normal", still writes things down. Sleeping normally. Driving again. Living with a roommate; seeing someone. No alcohol or drugs.

Exam: well appearing, cheerful, oriented, conversation normal. No abnormal movements. Heart and lungs normal.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 3.

A/P:
1. Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, recovering well off steroids. Neurology follow-up due in May; she has the number.
2. Ovarian teratoma, removed. Gyn to set up the yearly ultrasound.
3. CBC and CMP after the steroid course.
4. Physical due in April; combining with a fall visit instead since she was just here. Booked 9/15.
Flu up to date. Pap due 2027.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count, kidney, liver and sugar all normal. See you in September.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm at 114 beats per minute. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals within normal limits. No ST-segment or T-wave changes.

documents.title: Medicine Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
HOSPITAL MEDICINE, regional hospital
Admitted 4/25/2026 via the ED, discharged 4/28/2026

HPI: 23F with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis (2025, treated, ovarian teratoma removed) and a septic abortion (2024), no regular medications, NKDA. Roommate found her on the bathroom floor, confused and drowsy, about an hour after she swallowed a full bottle of an over-the-counter pain reliever following an argument with her partner. She had told the roommate she felt nauseated, dizzy and had ringing in her ears. No prior overdoses. Denies alcohol and drug use.

ED: BP 102/58, HR 115, RR 28, SpO2 98% RA. Drowsy but rousable, deep rapid respirations, pupils equal and reactive, no focal deficits, dry mucosa, capillary refill slightly prolonged, lungs clear, no signs of injury or injection.
ECG: sinus tachycardia.
The empty bottle was aspirin 325 mg. Salicylate 58 mg/dL; blood gas pH 7.46, pCO2 23; HCO3 16, anion gap 22, K 3.3. Acetaminophen undetectable. Urine drug screen negative, urine hCG negative, UA unremarkable.

Assessment: acute salicylate toxicity from intentional aspirin ingestion, mixed respiratory alkalosis and anion gap metabolic acidosis.

Course: MICU overnight. Sodium bicarbonate infusion with potassium repletion, urine alkalinized. Salicylate 39 at 6 hours and 17 the next morning; mental status cleared; dialysis not needed. Transferred to the floor 4/26, then medically cleared.
Psychiatry consult 4/27: impulsive ingestion in the setting of a fight with her partner; no ongoing intent to harm herself, future-oriented, supports in place. Safety plan completed with her and her mother; outpatient counseling referral placed.

Discharge medications: none.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 to 2 weeks; counseling intake as scheduled.

documents.title: hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. I have to tell you I was in the hospital last week, I took a bunch of aspirin after a fight with my boyfriend. It was stupid and I'm ok now. They set me up with a counselor. They said to follow up with you.

documents.title: Re: hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lauren, thank you for telling me. I'm glad you're safe. I'd like to see you next week, the front desk will call with a time. If you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself again, call or text 988 any time, or call our office line and ask for me. We'll get the hospital records.

documents.body: Pt called to cancel 11:00 today, picked up a shift. Says she is doing fine, saw the counselor once already. Wants to keep the 9/15 appointment rather than reschedule. Message sent to PCP.
